A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TtT research, with matching authors, architecture, and original experiments. Text extraction and visual inspection, including the complete appendices, support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original Audio-QA and ASR experiments, component ablations, and multimodal-pretraining comparisons in Table 1.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds external-model comparisons, audio-captioning results, and URO-Bench evaluations.

M1.justification: Both retain AR text generation, absorbing diffusion for audio, modality-aware attention, BANOM/PPM/SST, and the same block-wise inference algorithm. No replacement procedure or new component is described. Omitting the separate beta-weighted loss formula does not establish that the implemented training procedure changed.

E1.justification: v3 adds AAC evaluation on Clotho-v2 and MACS, already listed as training sources, and URO-Bench scenarios covering emotion, style, environmental sounds, music, and multi-round/multi-speaker dialogue. Training coverage is retained. v1 already reports LLaMAQuestions in Table 1, so its conflicting appendix entry for Chinese ReasoningQA does not establish an actual dataset substitution.

E2.justification: Tables 2–3 add evaluated comparisons with Moshi, SpeechGPT, Kimi-Audio, VITA-Audio, LLaMA-Omni, GLM-4-Voice, Mini-Omni, and SLAM-Omni. Some ASR entries are explicitly unavailable. The original controlled AR/NAR, ablation, and pretraining comparator sets remain in Table 1.

E3.justification: New protocols include CLAIR-A-style AAC scoring using Qwen3-30B-A3B on a 0–100 scale, and English URO-Bench evaluation with dataset/category averaging, a substituted Qwen3-30B-A3B judge, and NMOS/UTMOS metrics. Appendix A.7 documents these additions. Existing optimizer, decoding settings, and Audio-QA judges are retained.

E4.justification: The BANOM, PPM, and SST ablations and alignment-pretraining analysis retain their settings and results. The added AAC/URO-Bench tables are benchmark evaluations; explanations of comparator failures do not establish a separate diagnostic or robustness study.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: All 130 numerical entries in Table 1 remain identical. v3 adds extensive external-comparator, AAC, and URO-Bench results. Examples include Pretrain+TtT's AAC scores of 11.55/42.86 on Clotho/MACS and URO-Bench NMOS/UTMOS scores of 3.90/4.23. These are newly reported results, not improvements to the retained measurements.

T1.justification: The partial-order construction, order-marginalized likelihood, and Appendix A.1.1 upper-bound proof are retained. v3 removes the additional beta-weighted joint-loss definition in v1 Equation 21 while retaining the unweighted objective. This is a limited removal from the formal specification; most other mathematics is relocated or equivalently restated.

C1.justification: The central hybrid-model, theoretical-bound, and training-strategy contributions remain. The abstract and contribution list extend empirical superiority claims to AAC and speech-to-speech benchmarks, while dropping the explicit single-stage-training contribution and computational-cost framing.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 adds explanations involving missing ASR prompts, English-only comparator training, SLAM-Omni's separate AAC model, and Kimi-Audio's language inconsistencies. It also interprets performance relative to model size. Existing dependency and ablation interpretations remain, while Appendix A.5 newly asserts extensibility to other NAR methods.

D1.justification: v3 adds an anonymous source-code access statement where v1 only promises a future release, plus evaluation implementation information and URO-Bench sample counts. Existing training hyperparameters, hardware, inference settings, and data-format examples are retained, largely relocated into the appendix. Actual code accessibility is not established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: v3 adds comparator descriptions in Appendix A.8 and references for additional models, URO-Bench, captioning evaluation, and perceptual metrics; the CosyVoice reference is removed. The substantive related-work discussion in Appendix A.2 and the central hybrid AR–NAR positioning remain essentially unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, preliminaries, method explanations, and results narrative are extensively condensed and reorganized. Background theory and training details move into appendices, while the original ablation and pretraining sections become subsections of architectural validation alongside a new external-benchmarking section.

P2.justification: v3 adds two substantial comparison tables and a URO-Bench task inventory, expands the evaluation-dataset table with abbreviations, and moves the training/attention figure into the appendix. Captions, equation displays, and figure placement are extensively reformatted; the original diagrams and data-format examples largely retain their content.

improvement.justification: External comparisons, AAC/URO-Bench evaluation, and perceptual scores make v3 more informative about practical capabilities than v1's controlled comparisons alone. Clearer organization and reported code access also help. The net gain is limited by new overstatements: Section 4.3 claims superiority over SpeechGPT across Audio-QA, but Table 2 reports lower TriviaQA and WebQuestions scores. The appendix's substituted URO judge also qualifies the main text's claim of using the official protocol unchanged.
